YOUR TIME IS YOURS

A clearer view
of your data.

How the current Timeheld preview and this website handle information.

Last updated October 25, 2026

The Mac app in development

The current development version saves study history and preferences locally on your Mac. History includes the courses or projects you select, focus intervals and timestamps. The standalone preview does not include iCloud sync and does not upload this history to the Timeheld website.

Safari website protection

The extension uses the domains you choose to apply browser blocking rules while focus is active. Basic Safari blocking does not require all-sites access. Optional website permissions enable Timeheld’s custom blocked page. The current extension is not designed to inspect page contents or collect browsing history. Permissions can be managed in Safari settings.

Chrome, Edge and Firefox extensions (under development)

Chrome, Edge and Firefox extensions are under development and are not available to install yet. As currently designed, they use a local, read-only native connection. The Mac app shares only your selected domains, whether protection is active and a short expiry time. Account tokens, Premium codes and study history are not shared with these extensions.

The tabs permission lets the extension compare the addresses of open tabs with your selected domains and replace a distracting page when focus starts. Tab addresses, titles and page contents are not sent to the native helper or a server. The current expiring block list may be cached locally in the extension; browsing activity is not logged or saved.

These extensions and their helper make no network requests and contain no analytics. The helper reads a fixed, owner-private protection file. When the connection closes or the protection lease expires, the extension clears its rules as the browser processes the update. Browser scheduling and sleep can delay processing.

Extension permissions, private-window access and removal stay under your control in each browser. This section will be updated before any of these extensions becomes available.

Companion builds in development

Separate development builds support optional iCloud sync and iPhone/iPad companions. They can exchange settings, session control and study history using a private iCloud container. Those builds are not a public download, and public companion releases are not offered on this site.

CSV exports

Exported CSV files contain the history or summary data you choose to export. You choose where to save the file. Sharing a CSV elsewhere is your decision; exporting it does not upload it to this website.

This website

No advertising trackers, marketing analytics, account forms or email-signup forms have been added to this website. The hosting provider processes requests needed to deliver the site and may retain standard operational logs. Private previews may require the hosting platform’s sign-in.

External links

Links to Apple support open those providers’ websites. Their own privacy practices apply there.

Your controls

You can review local history in the app, manage Safari permissions in Safari settings, and decide whether to export your records. This page describes the current implementation and will be updated as public distribution and companion services develop.

Make the time count.
